 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice N.S.Sanjay Gowda)
1.
The insurer is in appeal challenging the liability imposed on it.
The claimant is also in appeal seeking for enhancement.

2. The insurer contends that there was a delay in lodging of the FIR and therefore this was a clear case of implication of the vehicle insured by it and therefore, it would not be responsible for the compensation.

3. The Tribunal has found that the claimant was initially admitted at the Shahpur Government hospital after he was transported in 108 ambulance where he was given first aid and thereafter he was shifted to Kalaburagi Kamareddy Hospital where he was admitted as an inpatient from 15.03.2015 to the 24.03.2015.
In this view of the matter, it is clear that the delay in lodging of the FIR on 02.04.2015 will have to be disregarded.

4. The insurer also contends that the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a driving license and despite NC: 2024:KHC-K:5861 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2022 a notice being issued in this regard, the same was not produced.

The Tribunal has taken note of the fact that the driver of the offending vehicle had not been charged by the police for driving without a license and it can be therefore presumed that he did possess a driving license.
5. In my view, this finding of the tribunal cannot be found fault with.
Consequently there is no merit in the appeal of the insurer and the same is dismissed.

6. As far as compensation is concerned, the tribunal has awarded the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Heads of Compensation  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of income/disability 2,44,800
2 . Pain and suffering 10,000
3. Food and nourishment 10,000  4. Transportation charges 10,000  5. Loss of amenities 10,000  6. Loss during treatment 5,000  7. Attendant charges 5,000  8.
Medical bills 26,531

Total 3,21,300/-

4  C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2022 7.

sentences.text: In awarding the above said sums, the tribunal has taken the monthly income at Rs.6,000/- and has assessed the disability at 20%.
In my view, the assessment of disability cannot be found fault with.
However, the fixation of the notional income of Rs.6,000/- will have to be modified, since the monthly notional income as per the chart prepared by KSLSA would be Rs.8,000/-.

Consequently,
the claimant will be entitled to Rs.3,26,400/- (8000x12x'17'x20%) towards 'loss of future income'.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.10,000 towards 'loss of amenities'.
In my view it will be appropriate to enhance the said sums to Rs.25,000/- each.

9. Having regard to the nature of the injuries suffered by him, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards food nourishment and conveyance charges, since the claimant was admitted for a period of nine days.

In my view the sums awarded by the Tribunal, are just and NC:
2024:KHC-K:5861 C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2022 proper and cannot be found fault with.
A sum of Rs.30,000/- towards 'food, nutrition, conveyance and attendant charges' is affirmed.
10. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.26,531/- towards 'medical expenses' and this being based on documentary evidence is affirmed.

Consequently, the claimant is entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Heads of Compensation  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of income/disability 3,26,400  2. Pain and suffering 25,000  Food, nutrition, conveyance  3. 30,000  and attendant charges  4. Loss of amenities 25,000  5.
Medical bills 26,531
